reviews.comment: Stiller reads verbatim off of lecture notes he got straight from the book, basically putting you to sleep. The exam is light years harder than the homework, averaging to be 20-24 questions which in pure math is bananas. He assigned homework covering 3 chapters of material we didn't cover in class. If you're a great math student, you might like him.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stiller should be kept from teaching in the math department until he learns basic technology. He refuses to publish a canvas, had trouble opening a PDF the first day, and doesn't know how to silence his phone. These hold him back from teaching at pace, and he "expects" us to learn many chapters ahead of his lectures to do homework when he's behind.
91% exam total that were super difficult, inaccuracies in lectures, lectures are not good, does not publish a canvas. Best thing he does are major curves exams like 20-30 points.

4 hard exams with insane curves. Also a slow HW grader: 2 classes before an exam I asked him whether we will get our HW back before the exam (b/c it had exam material on it) and he literally said no, I should have made a copy of it in case I wanted to study. Decent lecturer, and emails us the notes.

Graded by 4 exams and 6 homework assignments. He emailed notes and read them aloud in class, occasionally showing examples. Sometimes assumed we knew concepts. Homework grading was kinda slow, once returned after an exam having topics on it. Exams terrible with huge curves (12-30 pts). Could improve by being more engaging and giving practice exams.

Stiller's MATH 415 class:
-Refused to publish Canvas page for the course, keep track of your own grades and due dates.
-Homeworks are just problems taken from textbook, with slow grading. You won't have them back before exams.
-Unengaging monotone lectures, with handwritten notes that are ineligible and mistakes included
-Difficult exams, curves.

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Stiller did ok teaching the class, he undoubtedly found the material interesting and fun to teach.
whichever one of yall is rating this dude anything above a 1, hmu and lmk what kinda drugs yall are on

MATH 415: Worst. Lecturer. Ever. If you enjoy listening to boring and monotone lectures where someone reads you their notes for 75 minutes at once, you will like this class. The exams were extremely difficult and the homework rarely prepared you for them. The curves for his exams were beyond any that I had ever seen, one time being 33 points.

reviews.comment: Overall taught the class very well but your grade is basically determined by the midterms and final. He's a good lecturer but can be monotone during lectures. Also isn't very forgiving when it comes to issues on your end regard tech. However, exams are curved like 20+ points so the class definitely isn't impossible.

Prof. Stiller does not seem to get that there is a pandemic going on. Some of us do not have access to touch screen laptops or tablets, which places us at a massive disadvantage come test time, because he does not believe in giving students a couple extra minutes to print out the exams and quizzes. Forget about partial credit. It doesn't happen.

reviews.comment: I had him for MATH 470, he was a great professor and is very interesting to listen to... But don't let yourself think it will be easy, it takes a significant amount of effort to do well in his class. It will definitely not be an easy A, so study and do all the homework. (Also do all the problems on exams the way he taught you in lecture!)

reviews.comment: Peter Stiller made Linear Algebra my worst class in University. There is no partial credit on his assignments (aside from an occasional 2 points when you dont simplify). The test are incredibly difficult and there is no partial credit, and no calculators allowed in his class. Would not recommend as you will not enjoy this actually fun subject.

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer, covers a large amount of material each lecture and always gives good clarifications when asked. There were 7 quizzes, 1 project, and 4 exams including the final all but the project was heavily curved (on average 20 points). To pass the class it won't need much time but a decent amount of studying is needed for tests and quizzes.
This guy is totally brilliant.  The class was inspiring but I had to work hard to do well.
